findings.reason: recording `s16→s15` — for the same "both write the fence module" reason the author gave when adding `s17→s15` in the same commit — changes which nodes may run concurrently.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares only `s17→s15`, but §16 (heading at `:1539`, write paths at `:1549`) also writes `reckon/_worker_fence.py`, the module §15 holds, and its own open followup f-awcwyh-017 states that it "waits for §15, which holds `reckon/_worker_fence.py`"; both `s15` and `s16` are declared `implementable`, so a coordinator reading only the declaration map sees no edge and can dispatch them at once, where they collide on the same fence module

findings.reason: a node could add the probe, leave both copies of the rule in place, and still close §17, so the section's own named defect (two copies of the directory-creation rule that "can drift") would be delivered unmeasured; a falsifier for the consolidation — a test that intercepts `create_write_roots` and asserts the runtime-path creation goes through it — is what makes the deliverable match its measure.
findings.text: §17's deliverable has two halves (`create_node_tmp_runtime_paths` routed through `create_write_roots`, and a direct node-tmp probe added to the §15 test), but its done-when falsifies only the probe half: the negative control "removes the node-tmp seal from `fence_argv`" and reddens the probe, while the consolidation half is checked only by "the composed fence argv for a fixed set of roots is identical before and after the change", an assertion that holds whether or not the consolidation was made

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `create_write_roots` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:547`), `worker_scratch_seal_root` (`:1110`), `store_seal_keys` (`:1286`, used at `:1325`), `shared_store_seal_roots` (`:1143`), `_CodexDialect.argv` (`reckon/_backends.py:1203`, `--add-dir` loop at `:1222`–`:1228`) and `_fence_write_roots` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1916`) all resolve; §16's `reckon/_worker_fence.py:1322` is a three-line drift from the skip at `:1325` (same symbol, not a dangling pointer), and §17's `create_node_tmp_runtime_paths` exists only once §15 lands, which §17 declares as its `depends-on`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §17's done-when falsifies only the probe half of its deliverable; the rule-constant-creation half has no observable that can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15 and §17 place their gate logs under the run directory, the durable convention the §8–§14 gates also use, and no changed unit names a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `create_node_tmp_runtime_paths`, `fence_writable_roots` and the runtime-path list are named by mechanism; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or comment, and the `§N` references are plan structure, not code identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §15's seal of the node's `/tmp` follows its cited `rm -rf /tmp/tmp*` evidence and composes through the caller `_fence_write_roots` that §9 named; §16's root cause (codex declaring as writable the roots §10 seals) matches the cited `bwrap: Can't mkdir …/reports/.aws` evidence and its mechanism acts at the one `launch_plan`→`dialect.argv` call site (`reckon/_backends.py:2189`–`:2198`) that feeds every dialect; §17's consolidation follows §15's own review. Each mechanism is capable of producing its section's done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 seals the node's `/tmp`, §16 filters the codex writable roots, §17 routes the runtime-path creation through the existing rule and strengthens its probe; each names one capability, and a source file beside its test is this plan's normal shape (§9, §10, §11 alike).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §16 needs §15 to have landed, because both write `reckon/_worker_fence.py`, but `plan-section-depends-on` records only §17→§15.
